# Linkwright for Jira

> Linkwright for Jira is an Atlassian Forge app for Jira Cloud that links GitHub commits, branches, pull requests, reviews and deployments to Jira issues, feeds Jira's native Development panel, and shows for every repository how current its data is and why when it is not. Free for up to 10 users. Built by Linkwright, an independent developer in France.

Key facts:

- Works with Jira Cloud and GitHub.com. Not GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps (self-hosted GitLab is planned).
- Webhooks first, with a periodic check that rereads what webhooks missed; a Refresh button rereads a repository on demand.
- Per-repository sync state: Up to date, Out of date, Rate limited, Failing, Not authorized, with the time of the last webhook and of the last successful read.
- Checks five minutes after sending that Jira kept the links, and repairs the ones it dropped.
- Repositories are attached per Jira project.
- Measured on a real Jira Cloud site (30 September 2026): a commit reached the issue in 5.7 s; a 500-commit push arrived whole.
- Pricing: free up to 10 users; USD 2.61 per user per month from 11 to 100 users; USD 1.86 from 101 to 250.
- Runs on Atlassian Forge; no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification; aimed at self-service teams of 20 to 200 people.
- Status: on the Atlassian Marketplace (https://marketplace.atlassian.com/apps/1218910089), free for teams up to 10 users.

## Pages

- [Home](https://linkwright.io/): what it does, demo, pricing, limits, FAQ
- [Documentation](https://linkwright.io/docs.html): installation, linking rules, sync states, troubleshooting
- [GitHub commits not showing in Jira](https://linkwright.io/github-commits-not-showing-in-jira.html): a troubleshooting checklist that applies to any connector
- [GitHub for Jira alternatives](https://linkwright.io/github-for-jira-alternatives.html): the Marketplace options with public installs, ratings and prices
- [24 hours side by side with GitHub for Atlassian](https://linkwright.io/github-for-atlassian-side-by-side.html): the same pushes measured on both connectors (1–2 October 2026), including where the official app does better
- [Connect GitHub to Jira Cloud](https://linkwright.io/connect-github-to-jira-cloud.html): the setup steps
- [JQL for GitHub data in Jira](https://linkwright.io/jira-jql-development-github.html): which development[...] fields Jira Cloud accepts
- [Limit which GitHub repositories each Jira project can link](https://linkwright.io/restrict-github-repositories-per-jira-project.html): per-project and per-site repository boundaries, GitHub for Atlassian (JRACLOUD-99914), checklist
- [GitHub Issues vs Jira](https://linkwright.io/github-issues-vs-jira.html): both compared on vendor documentation (October 2026), when teams use both, and connecting them
- [GitHub for Jira backfill](https://linkwright.io/github-for-jira-backfill.html): what GitHub for Atlassian's backfill imports (Atlassian documentation, November 2026), how to continue or restart it, and a five-minute check
- [Jira Smart Commits with GitHub](https://linkwright.io/jira-smart-commits-github.html): syntax of #comment, #time and transitions (Atlassian documentation, November 2026), why a Smart Commit does not run (the commit email must match exactly one Jira user), a checklist, and how Linkwright limits who can run them
- [GitHub for Atlassian is moving to Forge](https://linkwright.io/github-for-atlassian-forge-migration.html): Atlassian's October 2026 rollout, and a before/after check of your development data
- [Atlassian Marketplace listing](https://marketplace.atlassian.com/apps/1218910089): install, pricing, reviews
- [Security](https://linkwright.io/security.html): data handled, architecture, vulnerability reporting
- [Privacy policy](https://linkwright.io/privacy.html)
